0GsiS1A1zHs.title: The Significance of Jumuah and Working Together
0GsiS1A1zHs.one_line: Why Jumuah anchors Muslim life, its etiquette and five purposes, and why masjids must serve first and raise support honestly.
0GsiS1A1zHs.summary: He returns to Jumuah because he senses attendance and respect for it dropped after COVID, and he addresses the youth who are off school that day. He walks through prophetic narrations on Friday as the weekly celebration: preparing with a shower, good clothes and scent, arriving early, not stepping over people, and listening in silence as if in prayer, with no talking or phones, while the angels close their records and sit to listen. He stresses that harming people on the way in, through careless driving or blocking them in, cancels the point, and that men, including students and employees, have no excuse to miss it. He then lists five purposes of Jumuah: leadership and shared vision, identity, remembrance of Allah, knowledge and clarity, and togetherness. If khutbahs fall short of these, the answer is to attend more and demand more. A residency story shows that rights not asked for are never granted. In the second part he follows the Prophet's practice of using the minbar to tell people where the community stands and what it needs. Masjids are places of service, not businesses that treat worshippers as dollar bills; an institution should serve first and read a lack of support as a sign it offers no value, and hotel galas with expensive tables are the wrong way to fund Muslim work.

outline.heading: Opening
Jumuah is our anchor
outline.gist: Without Jumuah Islam would not have spread as it did: two or three Muslims anywhere find a room and establish it, and communities grow from there. He senses a drop in attendance and respect since COVID and addresses the youth, off school today, above all.

outline.heading: The best of days: a weekly celebration
outline.gist: Friday is among the best of days: Adam was created and died on it, the Hour will come on it, and salawat on the Prophet are presented to him on it. We have two Eids a year but a celebration every week.

outline.heading: Not a sabbath: shower, dress, scent, come early
outline.gist: Allah needs no rest and work on Friday is not forbidden; the prayer is what is honoured. Whoever showers, wears good clothes and scent, comes early without pushing forward and listens to the imam is forgiven until the next Jumuah.

outline.heading: Silence: the khutbah is part of the prayer
outline.gist: Even telling your neighbour to be quiet ruins your Jumuah; communicate with no one but Allah and the imam, and no more check your phone than you would mid-prayer. The khutbah stands in for two of the four rakahs.

outline.heading: The angels at the doors
outline.gist: Angels sit at the masjid doors recording who arrives, when and how, close their records when the imam sits on the minbar, then come in to listen. Jumuah is one of the few times you can say with certainty that they are among you.

outline.heading: The latecomer who stepped over heads
outline.gist: A man came late while the Prophet was on the minbar, stepping beside people's heads to reach the front, and excused himself that he had only woken and made wudu; the excuse was not accepted, because Jumuah calls for a shower and coming early.

outline.heading: No harm on the way, no excuse for lateness
outline.gist: After the hour on Friday when every dua is accepted, he warns that harming people through how you park or drive is never made up for by the prayer. If you are late you carry the responsibility for not planning your day; men have no excuse.

outline.heading: Claim your Jumuah at school and work
outline.gist: Apart from rare cases such as a pilot or a surgeon mid-operation, you must pray and tell those around you it is your time of worship: a constitutional right and an Islamic obligation. Students should ask their schools for space and pray even with two or three.

outline.heading: Purpose one: leadership and a united vision
outline.gist: Jumuah was installed for leadership; the community's leader once used the minbar to give the plan and next steps so all shared a vision. Dysfunctional communities have no united vision, yet millions attend Jumuah weekly, where a little guidance could change lives.

outline.heading: Purpose two: identity
outline.gist: Jumuah is part of who you are as a Muslim, especially here; take your children out of school to attend it, because it shapes their identity.

outline.heading: Remembrance, knowledge and togetherness
outline.gist: Third, remembrance: after a busy week, a reminder of Allah's grace, forgiveness and love to bring the heart closer and re-evaluate your life. Fourth, knowledge: removing ambiguity so people understand their deen. Fifth, jama'ah: an intimate act done in a big, crowded group.

outline.heading: Never give up your right to Jumuah
outline.gist: If khutbahs have fallen short, attend more and demand more. Students and workers are not exempt. In residency he was told no Muslim doctor before him had asked for Jumuah time: ask, because unasked rights are lost for everyone after you, and protected time lets Jumuah be unhurried.

outline.heading: Interlude
Masjids are places of service
outline.gist: The Prophet used the Jumuah minbar to explain where the Muslims stood and where they needed to go. Masjids should not run as businesses that see worshippers as dollar bills and interrupt prayers to make people give; whoever works in a masjid has taken on serving those who come.

outline.heading: Interlude
Serve first, then ask
outline.gist: Religious institutions have a reputation for always asking for money, so the principle is to serve for a long time without a word about fundraising. If you then ask and support does not come, you are not offering value: go back to the drawing board or shut down.

outline.heading: Interlude
Say what you are doing and what you need
outline.gist: The Prophet simply told people what was being done and what was needed, and they gave what they could; that is how Medina, its homes and its defence were built. This is what the minbar is for.

outline.heading: No hotel galas
outline.gist: He rejects downtown hotel dinners with $150 tickets and $300 tables, open only to those who can afford them. Show people what you do and where you are going; if they believe in it they will support it, and if not, find out what they actually need.

outline.heading: Outro

WsHtQIfvNiI.title: Oppression on the Holy Land
WsHtQIfvNiI.one_line: A week into the Gaza bombing: keep the narrative simple and factual, recognize oppression first, then act politically and pass the cause to children.
WsHtQIfvNiI.summary: A week into the October 2023 bombing of Gaza, he says the world is not silent but openly backing the oppressor, including local politicians the community once welcomed. He sets three aims: restate the narrative, outline action, and talk about children. Borrowing the scholars' idea of identifying the actual point of dispute, he says a strong argument sticks to the point and ignores side issues: the 1917 promise, the 1948 expulsions, the 1967 occupation, illegal settlements and the siege are undisputed facts. Until someone condemns that, debating how the oppressed resist is unethical. Oppression grows like cancer and becomes darkness on the Day of Judgment, and justice is Islam's core value. This is not a Muslim-Jewish conflict; Jews lived among Muslims for centuries. He also apologizes to Muslims whose own oppression goes unmentioned. In the second khutbah he insists peace only counts if it serves justice, and lists actions: political pressure on the politicians the community supported, dua that is not a substitute for effort, donations, and raising awareness through freer media. Finally, children must be taught the narrative and given hope, and the Palestinian community in London needs support.

outline.heading: Opening
Worse than silence
outline.gist: For six or seven days the world has watched the bombing not in silence, which he would prefer, but with unwavering support for the oppressor, including local politicians the community welcomed into its masjids and voted in. It is the worst barbarity and hypocrisy he has seen in his lifetime.

outline.heading: Three aims for today
outline.gist: He is not there to deepen pain, anger or fear, but to restate the narrative, outline action plans, and talk about children. He starts from the scholars' notion of the point of dispute (mahall al-niza').

outline.heading: What is actually contested?
outline.gist: If you do not know what is disputed you cannot fix it, and the flood of TV opinions confuses people. He takes it back to simplicity; not living there, he will not judge how Palestinians should have acted.

outline.heading: A strong argument sticks to the point
outline.gist: He has not been treated as subhuman for fifty years and will not comment on internal Palestinian disagreements. Someone with a weak argument distracts with side issues or attacks your character; someone with a strong one sticks to the point.

In 1917 foreigners promised a land they did not own to people with no claim to it; in 1948 a Zionist state with birth-based citizenship ethnically cleansed towns and villages; in 1967 the Naksa occupied the rest. These are historical facts, not opinions.

outline.heading: Settlements and the siege
outline.gist: Settlements continue on land the whole world calls illegal, and a tiny, densely populated strip has been under siege for sixteen years. Beyond these undisputed facts, his opinion on anything else is irrelevant.

outline.heading: Condemn it first, then we can talk
outline.gist: Condemn Balfour, the Nakba, the Naksa and the decades of civilian deaths, and then he will discuss anything over lunch. Judging how the oppressed resist while the oppressor still holds what he took is unethical, philosophically and theologically.

outline.heading: Unacknowledged oppression is a cancer
outline.gist: Until the oppression is recognized there is nothing to discuss. Being oppressed while no one acknowledges it is unbearable; oppression is like cancer, growing until it is removed, and what goes around comes around.

outline.heading: Darkness on the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: Oppression grows in this world and becomes darkness on the Day of Judgment. Justice, standing against oppression, is Islam's core value and trumps every other.

outline.heading: Not Muslims against Jews
outline.gist: The issue is oppression, not a contest between Muslims and Jews, who have lived side by side as long as Muslims have existed. Middle Eastern cities still have Jewish quarters; Jews left Palestine with Muslims in the Crusades, returned with them, and left Andalusia with them.

outline.heading: We are sons of Ishmael
outline.gist: How can people who are sons and daughters of Ishmael be anti-Semitic? It is not about religion, and no civilian death anywhere is acceptable; the issue is an act of oppression begun a century ago, established 75 years ago and continuing, which Muslims will never let die.

outline.heading: Every oppression matters
outline.gist: Those who refuse to let the world forget them have every right. He apologizes to Muslims from other lands whose oppression he rarely speaks of; every Muslim's and every human being's oppression matters equally.

outline.heading: Carpet-bombing 2.2 million
outline.gist: Today's subject is what the world is watching and supporting: carpet-bombing a tiny strip while demanding that 2.2 million people relocate. Those in their fifties and sixties have seen it before; it is ongoing.

outline.heading: Interlude
Peace only if it serves justice
outline.gist: What can we do? First, keep the narrative clear: an apartheid state is occupying land illegally and carrying out ethnic cleansing to this day, and it must stop. Peace is only peace if it serves justice and returns Palestinians their rights; until then, unwavering solidarity.

outline.heading: Political advocacy
outline.gist: The most important action, and one his generation is bad at: the politicians the community supported must feel the loss of that support. Call, email and write, sticking to the basic narrative; it is the least we can do while Palestinians pay with their blood.

outline.heading: Dua is not doing something
outline.gist: Of course you make dua, as a Muslim does when he walks and sleeps and wakes. Telling Allah you are too busy and asking Him to fix it for you is not what dua is.

outline.heading: Donate
outline.gist: If you cannot do political work, support them financially; they will need a great deal and receive far less than they deserve.

outline.heading: Raise awareness; this is no side issue
outline.gist: Speak up in your circles. Muslims must be strategic about what they openly oppose and many issues can wait, but this is not one of them; do not be embarrassed, even if it costs us, because it costs them far more.

outline.heading: Use the freer media
outline.gist: Unlike the 1990s, when three or four outlets controlled information, the flow is now free enough for Muslims to put the narrative out themselves.

outline.heading: Pass the narrative to our children
outline.gist: Not only Gaza's children but ours: the narrative and the urgency of action must be taught at home and in the masjid, because a cause with people still standing for it does not die. He grew up without hope.

outline.heading: There is hope, and you are it
outline.gist: Al-Aqsa is central to Muslims; the Prophet journeyed there and ascended from it. He had little hope as a child, which is unhealthy: the young are the hope for public opinion to shift against the world's deliberate blindness, but there is too little work, advocacy and awareness on our side.

outline.heading: Interlude
Stand by London's Palestinian families
outline.gist: London has an unusually large Palestinian community. Call them and reach out, because unless you have watched your own country burn you cannot know how ugly that feeling is.

outline.heading: Outro

59:10.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ جَآءُو مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِمۡ يَقُولُونَ رَبَّنَا ٱغۡفِرۡ لَنَا وَلِإِخۡوَٰنِنَا ٱلَّذِينَ سَبَقُونَا بِٱلۡإِيمَٰنِ وَلَا تَجۡعَلۡ فِي قُلُوبِنَا غِلࣰّ ا لِّلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ رَبَّنَآ إِنَّكَ رَءُوفࣱ رَّحِيمٌ
59:10.en: And those who came (into the faith) after them say: Our Lord! Forgive us and our brethren who were before us in the faith, and place not in our hearts any rancour toward those who believe. Our Lord! Thou art Full of Pity, Merciful

59:11.ar: ۞أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِينَ نَافَقُواْ يَقُولُونَ لِإِخۡوَٰنِهِمُ ٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُواْ مِنۡ أَهۡلِ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَئِنۡ أُخۡرِجۡتُمۡ لَنَخۡرُجَنَّ مَعَكُمۡ وَلَا نُطِيعُ فِيكُمۡ أَحَدًا أَبَدࣰ ا وَإِن قُوتِلۡتُمۡ لَنَنصُرَنَّكُمۡ وَٱللَّهُ يَشۡهَدُ إِنَّهُمۡ لَكَٰذِبُونَ
59:11.en: Hast thou not observed those who are hypocrites, (how) they tell their brethren who disbelieve among the People of the Scripture: If ye are driven out, we surely will go out with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if ye are attacked we verily will help you. And Allah beareth witness that they verily are liars

59:12.ar: لَئِنۡ أُخۡرِجُواْ لَا يَخۡرُجُونَ مَعَهُمۡ وَلَئِن قُوتِلُواْ لَا يَنصُرُونَهُمۡ وَلَئِن نَّصَرُوهُمۡ لَيُوَلُّنَّ ٱلۡأَدۡبَٰرَ ثُمَّ لَا يُنصَرُونَ
59:12.en: (For) indeed if they are driven out they go not out with them, and indeed if they are attacked they help them not, and indeed if they had helped them they would have turned and fled, and then they would not have been victorious

59:8.ar: لِلۡفُقَرَآءِ ٱلۡمُهَٰجِرِينَ ٱلَّذِينَ أُخۡرِجُواْ مِن دِيَٰرِهِمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلِهِمۡ يَبۡتَغُونَ فَضۡلࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنࣰ ا وَيَنصُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلصَّٰدِقُونَ
59:8.en: And (it is) for the poor fugitives who have been driven out from their homes and their belongings, who seek bounty from Allah and help Allah and His messenger. They are the loyal

59:9.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ تَبَوَّءُو ٱلدَّارَ وَٱلۡإِيمَٰنَ مِن قَبۡلِهِمۡ يُحِبُّونَ مَنۡ هَاجَرَ إِلَيۡهِمۡ وَلَا يَجِدُونَ فِي صُدُورِهِمۡ حَاجَةࣰ مِّمَّآ أُوتُواْ وَيُؤۡثِرُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَنفُسِهِمۡ وَلَوۡ كَانَ بِهِمۡ خَصَاصَةࣱۚ وَمَن يُوقَ شُحَّ نَفۡسِهِۦ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡمُفۡلِحُونَ
59:9.en: Those who entered the city and the faith before them love those who flee unto them for refuge, and find in their breasts no need for that which hath been given them, but prefer (the fugitives) above themselves though poverty become their lot. And whoso is saved from his own avarice - such are they who are successful

Mq0hnNWFKno.title: Tafseer of Surat Al-Hashr, Part 4: Verses 10-12
Mq0hnNWFKno.one_line: Al-Hashr 10-12: the later generation's dua, respecting those who came first, disagreeing without hatred, and hypocrisy as refusing to commit.
Mq0hnNWFKno.summary: He recaps the surah as a model of citizenship in a mixed society and stresses that the Muslims of Medina were several groups who lived together without erasing their identities, a lesson for diverse Western masjids. Verse 10 names a third group, those who came later, and gives them a dua: forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and put no rancour in our hearts. Newcomers must respect seniority and acknowledge the good done before them instead of trashing history, while veterans must welcome change. Rancour locks the heart so it sees only faults. Ali grieving over Talha after a battle shows the companions fought without hatred, unlike today's viciousness over madhhabs, dead scholars and rival organisations, which he has felt personally. Verses 11-12 turn to the hypocrites who promised Banu al-Nadir support and lied. Hypocrisy is a spectrum that no one may use to label others, and its root is refusing to commit to anything. He urges young people to decide what they stand for, warns that Muslims who never truly contemplate their faith or death are unprepared when it comes, and notes the hypocrites stayed citizens while each person must decide which group they belong to.

outline.heading: The surah as a model of citizenship
outline.gist: Treason, the financial system and relations among Muslims so far; the Quran uniquely addresses living with people who differ from you and share your rights.

outline.heading: Three groups of Muslims in Medina
outline.gist: Even Muslims were not one homogeneous group, which sets a precedent for diverse communities not splitting into silos.

outline.heading: Living together without erasing identity
outline.gist: The Muhajirun lived in the Ansar's homes, yet both kept their identities and the Quran names them separately.

outline.heading: From a one-family village to a global community
outline.gist: In Syria nearly everyone at his masjid shared his surname; in Canada Muslims come from every continent, which is a gain.

outline.heading: Masjids open to all and differences acknowledged
outline.gist: People gravitate to their own, but a masjid must welcome everyone and respect different upbringings and ways of practising.

outline.heading: Reciting verse 10 after the sentimental verses
outline.gist: Unlike the legal passages, the verses on Muslims speak of love, sacrifice and loving immigrants rather than tolerating them.

outline.heading: A third group: those who came later
outline.gist: People who joined once things improved face the veterans' feeling that newcomers should sit back, a pattern in every institution.

outline.heading: The dua for those who preceded us in faith
outline.gist: Memorise this dua; late converts like those after the conquest of Mecca went on to lead, which only worked because of this culture.

outline.heading: Respecting seniority
outline.gist: Newcomers who declare everything done before them wrong are rarely right; seniority is not the only criterion for leadership but must carry weight.

outline.heading: We are the third group
outline.gist: Without this verse later Muslims would have no place in the model; every community has veterans, later arrivals and newcomers like him.

outline.heading: How communities go wrong, and the right dynamic
outline.gist: Either the builders are stripped of honour or newcomers are excluded; the first welcome, the later respect and pray for those before.

outline.heading: Do not trash all of history
outline.gist: Humanity keeps resetting as if everything before is garbage, but there is real ancient wisdom, which Muslims learned from and incorporated.

outline.heading: Ghill locks the heart and blinds it to good
outline.gist: Dislike makes you see only faults, as with feuding spouses; a community needs to see both good and bad.

outline.heading: Uthman refuses bloodshed on his account
outline.gist: Uthman forbade anyone to defend him, having been told by the Prophet he would choose between his life and the Muslims' lives.

outline.heading: Ali grieves over Talha
outline.gist: Even after fighting each other over Uthman's killers, Ali carried the dying Talha and prayed they would be among those whose hearts are cleansed of rancour.

outline.heading: No hatred over madhhabs or dead scholars
outline.gist: Disagree with opinions on their merit, but hating Muslims or historical figures who died centuries ago is a waste.

outline.heading: Disagreeing without demeaning; the most tender, the most merciful
outline.gist: The verse closes with the names al-Ra'uf al-Rahim, asking for tenderness to use with those we disagree with.

outline.heading: The endless struggle between old and new
outline.gist: Old and young always contend; the guideline is forgiveness and no hatred as the basis of the relationship.

outline.heading: Viciousness toward people who disagree
outline.gist: After he addressed a public controversy, people he had known for years said the cruellest things ever said about him over a difference in approach.

outline.heading: Beware viciousness toward other Muslim organisations
outline.gist: Toward competing institutions or people you dislike, keep objectivity and return to this dua.

outline.heading: Reciting verse 11: hypocrites and disbelievers
outline.gist: The surah now turns to the last groups of the city, judged by what they did and said.

outline.heading: Did you not see: knowing and contemplating
outline.gist: Ra'a with ila means did this not reach you and did you not reflect on it, not physical sight.

outline.heading: Hypocrisy as a spectrum
outline.gist: From working against Islam from inside to wanting only the cultural identity without commitment.

outline.heading: The four traits of a hypocrite
outline.gist: Lying, betraying trust, breaking promises and losing ethics in disputes; having one is a share of hypocrisy.

outline.heading: Never label others hypocrites
outline.gist: The traits are for self-accountability; calling a Muslim a hypocrite is as grave as calling him a disbeliever.

outline.heading: Hypocrites kept their citizenship
outline.gist: The Prophet knew them but did not expel them; Hudhayfah kept the names as insurance against them seizing power.

outline.heading: A brotherhood of disbelief
outline.gist: Their brothers are People of the Book bound by shared opposition; with them the whole fabric of the city is now named.

outline.heading: False promises to Banu al-Nadir
outline.gist: During the siege after the assassination plot, hypocrites promised to leave or fight with them, and Allah testifies they lie.

outline.heading: Hypocrisy is refusing to commit
outline.gist: A foot in each camp cannot last; the hypocrite backs whoever seems stronger to avoid effort, and life will eventually force a choice.

outline.heading: They will not leave and will turn their backs
outline.gist: When Banu al-Nadir were expelled the hypocrites stayed; an honest disbeliever is preferable to a hypocrite, who remains a burden but a citizen.

outline.heading: Decide what you stand for
outline.gist: Young people need core convictions; without any belief there is nothing to build a conversation on, and pinballing between sides is miserable.

outline.heading: Muslims who never contemplated their faith
outline.gist: Islam held only as theory leaves people unprepared, while some without faith have at least worked out a position.

outline.heading: 'I haven't lived yet': facing mortality
outline.gist: An elderly patient with a third cancer said he had not lived yet; making peace with mortality requires committing to a worldview.

outline.heading: Choose which group you belong to
outline.gist: Hypocrites and the remaining tribes stayed citizens; the surah asks each person where they stand in this diverse society.

outline.heading: Why the surah ends so beautifully
outline.gist: Some matters are governed by law and others by the ethics and brotherhood of faith, which the surah's closing verses express.

38:45.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عِبَٰدَنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ أُوْلِي ٱلۡأَيۡدِي وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
38:45.en: And make mention of Our bondmen, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, men of parts and vision

38:46.en: Lo! We purified them with a pure thought, remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter)

38:47.en: Lo! in Our sight they are verily of the elect, the excellent

38:48.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلۡيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلۡكِفۡلِۖ وَكُلࣱّ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَخۡيَارِ
38:48.en: And make mention of Ishmael and Elisha and Dhu'l-Kifl. All are of the chosen

38:49.ar: هَٰذَا ذِكۡرࣱۚ وَإِنَّ لِلۡمُتَّقِينَ لَحُسۡنَ مَـَٔابࣲ‏
38:49.en: This is a reminder. And lo! for those who ward off (evil) is a happy journey's end

38:50.en: Gardens of Eden, whereof the gates are opened for them

38:51.ar: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ فِيهَا يَدۡعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَٰكِهَةࣲ كَثِيرَةࣲ وَشَرَابࣲ‏
38:51.en: Wherein, reclining, they call for plenteous fruit and cool drink (that is) therein

38:52.en: And with them are those of modest gaze, companions

38:53.en: This it is that ye are promised for the Day of Reckoning

38:54.ar: إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَرِزۡقُنَا مَا لَهُۥ مِن نَّفَادٍ
38:54.en: Lo! this in truth is Our provision, which will never waste away

38:55.en: This (is for the righteous). And lo! for the transgressors there with be an evil journey's end

38:56.en: Hell, where they will burn, an evil resting-place

38:57.en: Here is a boiling and an ice-cold draught, so let them taste it

38:58.en: And other (torment) of the kind in pairs (the two extremes)

38:59.ar: هَٰذَا فَوۡجࣱ مُّقۡتَحِمࣱ مَّعَكُمۡ لَا مَرۡحَبَۢا بِهِمۡۚ إِنَّهُمۡ صَالُواْ ٱلنَّارِ
38:59.en: Here is an army rushing blindly with you. (Those who are already in the Fire say): No word of welcome for them. Lo! they will roast at the Fire

38:60.ar: قَالُواْ بَلۡ أَنتُمۡ لَا مَرۡحَبَۢا بِكُمۡۖ أَنتُمۡ قَدَّمۡتُمُوهُ لَنَاۖ فَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡقَرَارُ
38:60.en: They say: Nay, but you (misleaders), for you there is no word of welcome. Ye prepared this for us (by your misleading). Now hapless is the plight

38:61.ar: قَالُواْ رَبَّنَا مَن قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَٰذَا فَزِدۡهُ عَذَابࣰ ا ضِعۡفࣰ ا فِي ٱلنَّارِ
38:61.en: They say: Our Lord! Whoever did prepare this for us, oh, give him double portion of the Fire

38:62.ar: وَقَالُواْ مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَىٰ رِجَالࣰ ا كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَشۡرَارِ
38:62.en: And they say: What aileth us that we behold not men whom we were wont to count among the wicked

38:63.ar: أَتَّخَذۡنَٰهُمۡ سِخۡرِيًّا أَمۡ زَاغَتۡ عَنۡهُمُ ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ
38:63.en: Did we take them (wrongly) for a laughing-stock, or have our eyes missed them

38:64.ar: إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَحَقࣱّ تَخَاصُمُ أَهۡلِ ٱلنَّارِ
38:64.en: Lo! that is very truth: the wrangling of the dwellers in the Fire

38:65.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ مُنذِرࣱۖ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
38:65.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I am only a warner, and there is no Allah save Allah, the One, the Absolute

38:66.ar: رَبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا بَيۡنَهُمَا ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡغَفَّٰرُ
38:66.en: Lord of the heavens and the earth and all that is between them, the Mighty, the Pardoning

38:69.ar: مَا كَانَ لِيَ مِنۡ عِلۡمِۭ بِٱلۡمَلَإِ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰٓ إِذۡ يَخۡتَصِمُونَ
38:69.en: I had no knowledge of the Highest Chiefs when they disputed

38:70.ar: إِن يُوحَىٰٓ إِلَيَّ إِلَّآ أَنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ نَذِيرࣱ مُّبِينٌ
38:70.en: It is revealed unto me only that I may be a plain warner

12:24.ar: وَلَقَدۡ هَمَّتۡ بِهِۦۖ وَهَمَّ بِهَا لَوۡلَآ أَن رَّءَا بُرۡهَٰنَ رَبِّهِۦۚ كَذَٰلِكَ لِنَصۡرِفَ عَنۡهُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَٱلۡفَحۡشَآءَۚ إِنَّهُۥ مِنۡ عِبَادِنَا ٱلۡمُخۡلَصِينَ
12:24.en: She verily desired him, and he would have desired her if it had not been that he saw the argument of his Lord. Thus it was, that We might ward off from him evil and lewdness. Lo! he was of Our chosen slaves

17:14.ar: ٱقۡرَأۡ كِتَٰبَكَ كَفَىٰ بِنَفۡسِكَ ٱلۡيَوۡمَ عَلَيۡكَ حَسِيبࣰ ا
17:14.en: (And it will be said unto him): Read thy Book. Thy soul sufficeth as reckoner against thee this day

24:40.ar: أَوۡ كَظُلُمَٰتࣲ فِي بَحۡرࣲ لُّجِّيࣲّ يَغۡشَىٰهُ مَوۡجࣱ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ مَوۡجࣱ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ سَحَابࣱۚ ظُلُمَٰتُۢ بَعۡضُهَا فَوۡقَ بَعۡضٍ إِذَآ أَخۡرَجَ يَدَهُۥ لَمۡ يَكَدۡ يَرَىٰهَاۗ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَجۡعَلِ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ نُورࣰ ا فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن نُّورٍ
24:40.en: Or as darkness on a vast, abysmal sea. There covereth him a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud. Layer upon layer of darkness. When he holdeth out his hand he scarce can see it. And he for whom Allah hath not appointed light, for him there is no light

18:109.ar: قُل لَّوۡ كَانَ ٱلۡبَحۡرُ مِدَادࣰ ا لِّكَلِمَٰتِ رَبِّي لَنَفِدَ ٱلۡبَحۡرُ قَبۡلَ أَن تَنفَدَ كَلِمَٰتُ رَبِّي وَلَوۡ جِئۡنَا بِمِثۡلِهِۦ مَدَدࣰ ا
18:109.en: Say: Though the sea became ink for the Words of my Lord, verily the sea would be used up before the words of my Lord were exhausted, even though We brought the like thereof to help

39:73.ar: وَسِيقَ ٱلَّذِينَ ٱتَّقَوۡاْ رَبَّهُمۡ إِلَى ٱلۡجَنَّةِ زُمَرًاۖ حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءُوهَا وَفُتِحَتۡ أَبۡوَٰبُهَا وَقَالَ لَهُمۡ خَزَنَتُهَا سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُمۡ طِبۡتُمۡ فَٱدۡخُلُوهَا خَٰلِدِينَ
39:73.en: And those who keep their duty to their Lord are driven unto the Garden in troops till, when they reach it, and the gates thereof are opened, and the warders thereof say unto them: Peace be unto you! Ye are good, so enter ye (the Garden of delight), to dwell therein

7:20.ar: فَوَسۡوَسَ لَهُمَا ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ لِيُبۡدِيَ لَهُمَا مَا وُۥرِيَ عَنۡهُمَا مِن سَوۡءَٰتِهِمَا وَقَالَ مَا نَهَىٰكُمَا رَبُّكُمَا عَنۡ هَٰذِهِ ٱلشَّجَرَةِ إِلَّآ أَن تَكُونَا مَلَكَيۡنِ أَوۡ تَكُونَا مِنَ ٱلۡخَٰلِدِينَ
7:20.en: Then Satan whispered to them that he might manifest unto them that which was hidden from them of their shame, and he said: Your Lord forbade you from this tree only lest ye should become angels or become of the immortals

38:4.ar: وَعَجِبُوٓاْ أَن جَآءَهُم مُّنذِرࣱ مِّنۡهُمۡۖ وَقَالَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرُونَ هَٰذَا سَٰحِرࣱ كَذَّابٌ
38:4.en: And they marvel that a warner from among themselves hath come unto them, and the disbelievers say: This is a wizard, a charlatan

38:5.ar: أَجَعَلَ ٱلۡأٓلِهَةَ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدًاۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءٌ عُجَابࣱ‏
38:5.en: Maketh he the gods One Allah? Lo! that is an astounding thing

38:6.ar: وَٱنطَلَقَ ٱلۡمَلَأُ مِنۡهُمۡ أَنِ ٱمۡشُواْ وَٱصۡبِرُواْ عَلَىٰٓ ءَالِهَتِكُمۡۖ إِنَّ هَٰذَا لَشَيۡءࣱ يُرَادُ
38:6.en: The chiefs among them go about, exhorting: Go and be staunch to your gods! Lo! this is a thing designed

38:7.ar: مَا سَمِعۡنَا بِهَٰذَا فِي ٱلۡمِلَّةِ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ إِنۡ هَٰذَآ إِلَّا ٱخۡتِلَٰقٌ
38:7.en: We have not heard of this in later religion. This is naught but an invention

38:8.ar: أَءُنزِلَ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلذِّكۡرُ مِنۢ بَيۡنِنَاۚ بَلۡ هُمۡ فِي شَكࣲّ مِّن ذِكۡرِيۚ بَل لَّمَّا يَذُوقُواْ عَذَابِ
38:8.en: Hath the reminder been unto him (alone) among us? Nay, but they are in doubt concerning My reminder; nay but they have not yet tasted My doom

mcDZuvnMi3o.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Sad, Remembrance of the Home, Paradise and the Quarrel of the People of the Fire (38:45-70)
mcDZuvnMi3o.one_line: Allah purifies His prophets through constant remembrance of the Hereafter; the surah then shows paradise for the God-conscious and hell for those who never admit fault.
mcDZuvnMi3o.summary: He explains what made all the prophets quick to return to the truth: Allah purified them with 'remembrance of the Home'. Sincerity cannot be produced by effort alone; Allah grants something pure, and a heart tied to the Hereafter sheds its attachments because nothing compares to that Day. This answers our feeling that the stories of Dawud, Sulayman and Ayyub are beyond us. The surah then describes the good return of the God-conscious: gardens of abundance whose gates stand open before they arrive, reclining at ease, calling for fruit, spouses of their own age who look only at them, and provision that never runs out. He reflects that life in this world is precious because it ends, while the next life is the true provision and endless. For the tyrants, whom he defines as wrongdoers whose pride stops them returning, the return is hell, boiling water and pus, and endless quarrelling: even in the Fire they blame one another and only briefly wonder whether the believers they mocked were right. He urges listeners to turn the Day of Judgment from an idea into a value, asking of every choice whether it will ease or worsen their reckoning. The passage closes with the Prophet as a warner and Allah as the One, the Overpowering, the Forgiving.

outline.heading: What unites the famous and the little-known prophets
outline.gist: Ibrahim and Dhul-Kifl alike returned to the truth without pride; the question is how.

outline.heading: Sincerity is granted, not manufactured
outline.gist: You cannot make yourself sincere; you correct your intention and Allah makes you mukhlas if He wills.

outline.heading: 'With a pure thing', not 'with a purifier'
outline.gist: The wording means Allah gave them something pure, and tasting that purity helped them become sincere.

outline.heading: A heart tied to the Hereafter
outline.gist: They live, study, earn and socialise, but their hearts are attached to that Home; its terror leaves no room for clinging to wealth or status.

outline.heading: Remembering the Hereafter removes the rust of the heart
outline.gist: Nothing cleanses like attachment to the next life; death alone does not, unless you remember what follows it.

outline.heading: The Reckoning is no game
outline.gist: You will be asked about your life, work and wealth and told to read your own book, which you wrote with your deeds.

outline.heading: Why this passage: we feel unable to copy them
outline.gist: The three stories leave us feeling helpless before such character; this verse names the means by which they did it.

outline.heading: The trait that brings openings, and how falsehood piles up
outline.gist: Every story ended with Allah opening for them; falsehood is darkness upon darkness, starting with one small mistake.

outline.heading: 'This is a reminder': the good return of the God-conscious
outline.gist: Recitation begins; fronting 'for the muttaqin' stresses who receives the reward.

outline.heading: Read the Quran's language with Zamakhshari and Baydawi
outline.gist: Word order changes carry purpose; Al-Kashshaf is superb on language though its author was a Mu'tazili.

outline.heading: Reciting qasirat: keep the ta' light
outline.gist: Surrounded by heavy letters, the ta' is easily thickened; a classic test point.

outline.heading: Nafad, not nafadh
outline.gist: Nafad with dal means running out; nafadh with dhal means piercing through, a common mistake.

outline.heading: Ma'ab answers awwab
outline.gist: Everything so far in the surah is a reminder; those who keep returning to Allah are given a good place of return.

outline.heading: Taqwa is what brings you back
outline.gist: Taqwa means asking whether this choice protects me from Allah's punishment on that Day; that question makes return quick.

outline.heading: 'Adn: gardens of abundance
outline.gist: 'Adn means plenty and yield, the Eden of earlier scriptures; he notes the meaning of his own name.

outline.heading: Gates already open
outline.gist: Complete honour means arriving to an open door rather than knocking and waiting.

outline.heading: The Prophet knocks first on the gate of Paradise
outline.gist: The keeper opens only for him, and seventy thousand enter without reckoning, then others like full moons and stars.

outline.heading: Paradise comforts the soul, not only the body
outline.gist: The Quran describes emotional ease too: nothing is closed to you and you are welcomed.

outline.heading: Reclining and calling for what they wish
outline.gist: Reclining symbolises rest from labour; they call and are served, not a self-serve buffet.

outline.heading: Fruit means food for enjoyment
outline.gist: Fakihah is eaten for pleasure, not hunger, as the Arabs enjoyed fruit before and after meals.

outline.heading: Spouses of the same age who look only at you
outline.gist: Marriages of similar age bring harmony; spouses with lowered gaze mean no betrayal.

outline.heading: This is the real provision
outline.gist: All worldly provision is like the drop on a needle dipped in the sea; this is what to chase.

outline.heading: Provision that never runs out
outline.gist: The mind struggles with endlessness; Allah offers the eternity Iblis falsely promised Adam.

outline.heading: This life is precious because it ends
outline.gist: Without death time and deeds would lose value; loss gives our time with others its worth.

outline.heading: Your name is written on every drop
outline.gist: A drop travels from the ocean through rain and bottling to reach you; worldly provision is counted, the next is not.

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 55-61
outline.gist: Including the Kufan reading ghassaq with a doubled sin.

outline.heading: 'This': a firm transition
outline.gist: The repeated 'hadha' confirms what was said and moves to the next point, as news presenters do.

outline.heading: Turn the Day of Judgment from an idea into a value

outline.heading: Tughyan: wrongdoing joined with pride

outline.heading: Jahannam: brought to it against their will

outline.heading: Boiling water, pus and more of the same
outline.gist: Their 'fruit and drink' is hamim and ghassaq and other punishments of the same kind.

outline.heading: Back to the opening: now they taste it
outline.gist: The surah began with them calling the Prophet a lying sorcerer 'for they have not yet tasted punishment'.

outline.heading: Even in the Fire they blame others
outline.gist: Each group curses the other and asks Allah to double the other's punishment; none can blame himself.

outline.heading: Most people need proof before admitting fault
outline.gist: The prophets blamed themselves unprompted; most people need it shown in sound and picture and still find excuses.

outline.heading: 'Why do we not see the men we counted as bad?'
outline.gist: For a moment they wonder whether those they mocked were better, or are just out of sight, and then the story ends.

outline.heading: The quarrel of the people of the Fire is real

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 65-70: 'ana' in waqf and wasl
outline.gist: The alif of ana is pronounced when stopping and dropped when joining, marked by the oval sign.

outline.heading: 'I am only a warner'
outline.gist: The Prophet's task is to make clear what endangers you.

outline.heading: The One: oneness is how we know Allah
outline.gist: He is one in names, attributes and acts; with a partner, people would be torn between them.

outline.heading: Al-Qahhar: our choice is only temporary
outline.gist: Everything is subdued to Him and on that Day all will obey; this should keep us humble.

outline.heading: A great news people turn away from
outline.gist: The Mighty and Forgiving Lord; this news, if grasped, would be the pure thing that purifies.

outline.heading: No knowledge of the exalted assembly except by revelation
outline.gist: The Prophet knows of the dispute over Adam only through revelation, leading into the story of Iblis.

38:41.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عَبۡدَنَآ أَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ بِنُصۡبࣲ وَعَذَابٍ
38:41.en: And make mention (O Muhammad) of Our bondman Job, when he cried unto his Lord (saying): Lo! the devil doth afflict me with distress and torment

38:42.ar: ٱرۡكُضۡ بِرِجۡلِكَۖ هَٰذَا مُغۡتَسَلُۢ بَارِدࣱ وَشَرَابࣱ‏
38:42.en: (And it was said unto him): Strike the ground with thy foot. This (spring) is a cool bath and a refreshing drink

38:43.ar: وَوَهَبۡنَا لَهُۥٓ أَهۡلَهُۥ وَمِثۡلَهُم مَّعَهُمۡ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنَّا وَذِكۡرَىٰ لِأُوْلِي ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
38:43.en: And We bestowed on him (again) his household and therewith the like thereof, a mercy from Us, and a memorial for men of understanding

38:44.ar: وَخُذۡ بِيَدِكَ ضِغۡثࣰ ا فَٱضۡرِب بِّهِۦ وَلَا تَحۡنَثۡۗ إِنَّا وَجَدۡنَٰهُ صَابِرࣰ اۚ نِّعۡمَ ٱلۡعَبۡدُ إِنَّهُۥٓ أَوَّابࣱ‏
38:44.en: And (it was said unto him): Take in thine hand a branch and smite therewith, and break not thine oath. Lo! We found him steadfast, how excellent a slave! Lo! he was ever turning in repentance (to his Lord)

38:45.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ عِبَٰدَنَآ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ وَإِسۡحَٰقَ وَيَعۡقُوبَ أُوْلِي ٱلۡأَيۡدِي وَٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرِ
38:45.en: And make mention of Our bondmen, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, men of parts and vision

38:46.en: Lo! We purified them with a pure thought, remembrance of the Home (of the Hereafter)

38:47.en: Lo! in Our sight they are verily of the elect, the excellent

38:48.ar: وَٱذۡكُرۡ إِسۡمَٰعِيلَ وَٱلۡيَسَعَ وَذَا ٱلۡكِفۡلِۖ وَكُلࣱّ مِّنَ ٱلۡأَخۡيَارِ
38:48.en: And make mention of Ishmael and Elisha and Dhu'l-Kifl. All are of the chosen

38:24.ar: قَالَ لَقَدۡ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعۡجَتِكَ إِلَىٰ نِعَاجِهِۦۖ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡخُلَطَآءِ لَيَبۡغِي بَعۡضُهُمۡ عَلَىٰ بَعۡضٍ إِلَّا ٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْ وَعَمِلُواْ ٱلصَّٰلِحَٰتِ وَقَلِيلࣱ مَّا هُمۡۗ وَظَنَّ دَاوُۥدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّٰهُ فَٱسۡتَغۡفَرَ رَبَّهُۥ وَخَرَّۤ رَاكِعࣰ اۤ وَأَنَابَ۩
38:24.en: (David) said: He hath wronged thee in demanding thine ewe in addition to his ewes, and lo! many partners oppress one another, save such as believe and do good works, and they are few. And David guessed that We had tried him, and he sought forgiveness of his Lord, and he bowed himself and fell down prostrate and repented

21:83.ar: ۞وَأَيُّوبَ إِذۡ نَادَىٰ رَبَّهُۥٓ أَنِّي مَسَّنِيَ ٱلضُّرُّ وَأَنتَ أَرۡحَمُ ٱلرَّٰحِمِينَ
21:83.en: And Job, when he cried unto his Lord, (saying): Lo! adversity afflicteth me, and Thou art Most Merciful of all who show mercy

21:84.en: Then We heard his prayer and removed that adversity from which he suffered, and We gave him his household (that he had lost) and the like thereof along with them, a mercy from Our store, and a remembrance for the worshippers

33:37.ar: وَإِذۡ تَقُولُ لِلَّذِيٓ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِ وَأَنۡعَمۡتَ عَلَيۡهِ أَمۡسِكۡ عَلَيۡكَ زَوۡجَكَ وَٱتَّقِ ٱللَّهَ وَتُخۡفِي فِي نَفۡسِكَ مَا ٱللَّهُ مُبۡدِيهِ وَتَخۡشَى ٱلنَّاسَ وَٱللَّهُ أَحَقُّ أَن تَخۡشَىٰهُۖ فَلَمَّا قَضَىٰ زَيۡدࣱ مِّنۡهَا وَطَرࣰ ا زَوَّجۡنَٰكَهَا لِكَيۡ لَا يَكُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ حَرَجࣱ فِيٓ أَزۡوَٰجِ أَدۡعِيَآئِهِمۡ إِذَا قَضَوۡاْ مِنۡهُنَّ وَطَرࣰ اۚ وَكَانَ أَمۡرُ ٱللَّهِ مَفۡعُولࣰ ا
33:37.en: And when thou saidst unto him on whom Allah hath conferred favour and thou hast conferred favour: Keep thy wife to thyself, and fear Allah. And thou didst hide in thy mind that which Allah was to bring to light, and thou didst fear mankind whereas Allah hath a better right that thou shouldst fear Him. So when Zeyd had performed that necessary formality (of divorce) from her, We gave her unto thee in marriage, so that (henceforth) there may be no sin for believers in respect of wives of their adopted sons, when the latter have performed the necessary formality (of release) from them. The commandment of Allah must be fulfilled

1O5EG6dJmRI.title: Arabic Tafsir: Surat Sad, Ayyub and the Chosen Prophets (38:41-48)
1O5EG6dJmRI.one_line: Ayyub admits a hasty oath despite eighteen years of suffering; returning to truth is a gift Allah grants through remembering the Hereafter.
1O5EG6dJmRI.summary: Ayyub lost family, wealth, standing and health for eighteen years and only praised Allah, too shy even to ask for relief. When his wife complained and he swore in anger to strike her, he saw the oath as his own wrong and said Shaytan had touched him with hardship, offering no excuse. Relief came at once: a spring to wash and drink from, his family restored and doubled, and a bundle of grass so he could keep his oath without harming her. He compares the three stories: Dawud, Sulayman and Ayyub each had every excuse and used none, and each was honoured right after returning. Sins are weighed by the One you disobey, so for the self no sin is small, and an unadmitted small mistake becomes a stance, then an identity, then a cause, which is how most misguidance happens; Iblis, at the end of the surah, is the opposite case. Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub had power and insight because Allah purified them with remembrance of the Home: the ability to return is a gift from Allah, and remembering the Hereafter is how to seek it. All the prophets shared this, which he calls the secret of prophethood.

outline.heading: Ayyub lost everything and only praised Allah
outline.gist: We sink into gloom over one loss; for eighteen years he kept praising and would not even ask for relief.

outline.heading: 'Shaytan has touched me with hardship': owning the oath
outline.gist: His gentle plea admits that his angry oath was his own wrong, prompted by Shaytan; he admitted it the moment it left his mouth.

outline.heading: 'Strike with your foot': the spring that healed him
outline.gist: He ran to a cool spring, washed and drank, and the illness left his skin and body.

outline.heading: Family restored and doubled, a reminder for the wise
outline.gist: Each of the three stories ends with this lesson: relief comes to those who return to the truth at once.

outline.heading: A sin is weighed by the One you disobeyed
outline.gist: The small-major division is a legal category; in purifying the self every sin is major because Allah is great.

outline.heading: What to do about the oath
outline.gist: He admitted the oath was a mistake; the next verse gives the way out.

outline.heading: Recitation of verses 44-48 with tajweed notes
outline.gist: The ba' of fadrib merges into the next ba' in Hafs; how to stop on it.

outline.heading: Al-mustafayn: a plural, not a dual
outline.gist: The nun is open because it is a sound masculine plural of mustafa, not a dual.

outline.heading: The bundle of grass: keeping an oath that should not have been made
outline.gist: There was no expiation in his law, so he was told to strike with a bundle of grass; Allah did not let him carry out the oath, which shows it was wrong.

outline.heading: Layer upon layer of patience
outline.gist: Picture losing your family, strength, money and status while your wife works to feed you; one slip in that state would be easy to excuse.

outline.heading: His wife's complaint and his anger for Allah's sake
outline.gist: He was angry not over food or the house but because he thought she objected to Allah's decree; he still treated his oath as his fault.

outline.heading: Three prophets, three excuses not taken
outline.gist: Dawud's intruders, Sulayman's good intentions and Ayyub's suffering could all justify them; none of them used it.

outline.heading: Honour came right after each return
outline.gist: Sulayman's kingdom and Dawud's title of khalifah followed directly on their repentance.

outline.heading: The surah is not about the mistakes
outline.gist: Mistakes are part of being human; the question is whether pride lets you return.

outline.heading: How a small mistake becomes misguidance
outline.gist: Unadmitted, it becomes a habit, then a stance, an identity, a reputation and a cause; most misguidance happens this way.

outline.heading: Iblis at the end of the surah: the other path
outline.gist: Three matching examples of returning are followed by one opposite one: be like the prophets or like the accursed.

outline.heading: The Prophet corrected by revelation
outline.gist: Even passing thoughts of the Prophet were addressed by the Quran, such as the permission he gave the hypocrites and leaning towards Quraysh.

outline.heading: Recap: Dawud's slip and judging by effort, not outcome
outline.gist: Even if Dawud's verdict was right, he still had to hear the other side; what counts is doing the work properly.

outline.heading: Ibrahim, Ishaq and Ya'qub: power and insight
outline.gist: Like Dawud's strength, they had capability and standing, and insight to tell truth from falsehood.

outline.heading: Purified by Allah: returning is His gift
outline.gist: 'We purified them with a pure quality': the ability to return to the truth comes from Allah, not from our own effort.

outline.heading: Mukhlasin: made sincere by Allah
outline.gist: Yusuf is called mukhlas: Allah makes you sincere once you show Him desire, repentance and resolve.

outline.heading: Remembrance of the Home
outline.gist: Remembering the Hereafter is what helps you return; the coming verses describe it vividly.

outline.heading: Next to the Hereafter, worldly pride is nothing
outline.gist: Without comparison the world fills the eyes; with it reputation and status shrink and returning becomes easy.

outline.heading: Start by remembering the Reckoning often
outline.gist: If we do, Allah may purify us as He purified the prophets; they were chosen and among the best.

outline.heading: Isma'il, al-Yasa' and Dhul-Kifl: the secret of prophethood
outline.gist: Listing prophets we know little about tells us all of them shared this; returning to the truth is the secret of prophethood.

outline.heading: Al-akhyar: wholly good
outline.gist: A word found only here: those who never persist in falsehood are entirely good.

outline.heading: Outro
